title: Storage firewalls, virtual network rules and private endpoints
learningObjective: Restrict a storage account to specific public IPs, subnets and private endpoints, and predict which clients can connect.
foundation: By default a storage account accepts connections from any network, as long as the request is authorised. The storage firewall lets you narrow that down.
You can allow specific public IP addresses (your office), specific subnets of your virtual networks, or turn public access off completely and use private endpoints.
The network check happens first. Even with a valid key or SAS token, a request from a blocked network gets 403.
engineer: Public network access: Enabled from all networks; Enabled from selected virtual networks and IP addresses (default action Deny plus allow rules); or Disabled (only private endpoints work).

IP network rules accept public IPv4 addresses and ranges only (no RFC 1918 ranges). /31 and /32 prefixes are not supported (enter single addresses without a prefix), and there are up to 400 IP rules. IP rules have no effect on requests from Azure services in the same region, which use private Azure addresses; use VNet rules, private endpoints, resource instance rules or the trusted services exception instead.

Virtual network rules allow a subnet. The subnet must have the Microsoft.Storage (or Microsoft.Storage.Global) service endpoint, which routes traffic over the Azure backbone with the subnet's identity while still using the storage account's public endpoint.

Private endpoints give the account a private IP from your VNet (one endpoint per sub-resource: blob, file, dfs, queue, table, web). Traffic through a private endpoint is not evaluated by the firewall. DNS must resolve <account>.blob.core.windows.net to the private IP, normally through the privatelink.blob.core.windows.net private DNS zone.

Exceptions: allow Azure services on the trusted services list (for example Azure Backup, Event Grid, Azure Monitor diagnostic logs), allow read access to logging/metrics, and resource instance rules for specific resources by resource ID.
Firewall rules apply to every protocol, including SMB to Azure Files and REST. They also apply to the portal: browsing data from a blocked client IP fails even for Owners.

example.title: Locking down a data account
body: A finance storage account is reachable only from the app subnet (service endpoint plus VNet rule) and the head-office public IP range. Azure Backup still works because 'Allow trusted Azure services' is on.

Later the security team disables public network access entirely and adds private endpoints for blob and file, with private DNS zones linked to the hub VNet. On-premises clients reach it over ExpressRoute using the private IPs.

prerequisites: Subnet service endpoint Microsoft.Storage for VNet rules
Private DNS zone for private endpoints
permissions: Storage Account Contributor (or Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/write) to change network rules
limits: IP rules accept public addresses only
IP rules do not apply to same-region Azure traffic
portal: Storage account > Security + networking > Networking > Firewalls and virtual networks: Public network access = Enabled from selected virtual networks and IP addresses.
Add existing virtual network: pick the VNet and subnet (the portal can enable the service endpoint).
Firewall: add IP addresses or CIDR ranges; optionally 'Add your client IP address'.
Exceptions: Allow Azure services on the trusted services list.
Private endpoint connections > + Private endpoint: choose the target sub-resource (blob, file…) and integrate with a private DNS zone.
configuration.cli:
az network vnet subnet update -g rg-net --vnet-name vnet-prod -n snet-app --service-endpoints Microsoft.Storage
az storage account update -g rg-data -n stcontoso --default-action Deny --bypass AzureServices
az storage account network-rule add -g rg-data --account-name stcontoso --ip-address 203.0.113.0/24
az storage account network-rule add -g rg-data --account-name stcontoso --vnet-name vnet-prod --subnet snet-app
az network private-endpoint create -g rg-net -n pe-stcontoso-blob --vnet-name vnet-prod --subnet snet-pe \
  --private-connection-resource-id $(az storage account show -g rg-data -n stcontoso --query id -o tsv) \
  --group-id blob --connection-name pe-stcontoso-blob
az storage account update -g rg-data -n stcontoso --public-network-access Disabled
configuration.powershell:
Update-AzStorageAccountNetworkRuleSet -ResourceGroupName rg-data -Name stcontoso -DefaultAction Deny -Bypass AzureServices
Add-AzStorageAccountNetworkRule -ResourceGroupName rg-data -Name stcontoso -IPAddressOrRange '203.0.113.0/24'
$subnet = Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName rg-net -Name vnet-prod | Get-AzVirtualNetworkSubnetConfig -Name snet-app
Add-AzStorageAccountNetworkRule -ResourceGroupName rg-data -Name stcontoso -VirtualNetworkResourceId $subnet.Id

lab.objective: Allow exactly the intended networks and explain each 403.
steps: Send a read from the internet client 198.51.100.20 with a valid SAS. It is blocked by the firewall.
Send from the VM in snet-app. It is blocked until you tick the VNet rule.
Try adding 10.0.0.0/16 as an IP rule and read the validation error.
Set public network access to Disabled and send through the private endpoint.
expected: 403 at the network layer before authorization
VNet rule plus service endpoint allows the subnet
The private endpoint works with public access disabled

validation.text: Saw a request blocked by network rules
Allowed a subnet with a VNet rule
Reached the account through a private endpoint with public access disabled

failureScenarios: Private IP range in IP rules
VNet rule without a service endpoint
lab.cost: None in the simulation. Private endpoints are billed per hour and per GB processed.

troubleshooting.symptom: Portal shows 'This request is not authorized to perform this operation' for an Owner.
troubleshooting.cause: The client IP is blocked by the storage firewall.
troubleshooting.fix: Add your client IP, or use a VM or private endpoint inside an allowed network.

troubleshooting.symptom: An App Service in the same region cannot reach storage despite an IP rule for its outbound IP.
troubleshooting.cause: IP rules do not apply to same-region Azure traffic.
troubleshooting.fix: Use VNet integration plus a service endpoint or private endpoint.

troubleshooting.symptom: A VM resolves the public IP even though a private endpoint exists.
troubleshooting.cause: Private DNS zone not linked to the VNet, or custom DNS not forwarding.
troubleshooting.fix: Link privatelink.blob.core.windows.net to the VNet or configure conditional forwarding.

troubleshooting.symptom: Azure Backup of a file share fails after enabling the firewall.
troubleshooting.fix: Enable 'Allow Azure services on the trusted services list'.

comparisons.difference: Service endpoints keep the public endpoint but identify the subnet; private endpoints give a private IP, and can be reached from peered VNets and on-premises.

comparisons.service: Amazon S3 bucket policies with aws:SourceVpce
comparisons.difference: AWS restricts by VPC endpoint in a resource policy; Azure uses account-level network rules.

misconceptions.myth: A valid account key bypasses the firewall.
misconceptions.reality: Network rules are evaluated first, for every authorization method.

misconceptions.myth: Service endpoints give the storage account a private IP.
misconceptions.reality: Only private endpoints do; service endpoints still use the public endpoint.

misconceptions.myth: You can allow 10.0.0.0/8 in the IP firewall.
misconceptions.reality: IP rules accept public addresses only.

architectureDecisions: Prefer private endpoints plus public access Disabled for sensitive data.
Use service endpoints for simple VNet-only access within a region when private IPs and DNS are not needed.
Keep the trusted services exception on when you rely on Azure Backup, Monitor or Event Grid.

walkthrough.subtitle: By default anyone on the internet can reach your storage account's front door. Close it, and open it only for who needs it.
learn: Public network access: all, selected, disabled
Virtual network rules and IP rules

steps.label: Open door
steps.title: Your storage account answers the whole internet
body: A new storage account accepts connections from every network. Keys and permissions still protect the data, but one leaked key exposes everything.

steps.label: Firewall
steps.title: Turn on the storage firewall
body: Networking > Public network access: Enabled from all networks, Enabled from selected virtual networks and IP addresses, or Disabled.
With 'selected', only the networks and IP ranges you list can connect.

steps.label: Rules
steps.title: Add who is allowed
body: IP rules allow public IP addresses or ranges, such as your office. Virtual network rules allow subnets in Azure; they rely on a service endpoint for Microsoft.Storage on that subnet.
The exception 'Allow Azure services on the trusted services list' lets services such as Azure Backup in.

callout.text: The portal's file and blob browser also connects from your IP. Lock the account down without adding your IP, and you cannot browse your own data in the portal.

steps.label: Private
steps.title: Go fully private with a private endpoint
body: A private endpoint gives the storage account a private IP inside your VNet. Combine it with Public network access: Disabled and nothing on the internet can reach it at all.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Storage network access
body: Close the door, then open it for named networks.
recap: IP rules for public addresses; VNet rules via service endpoints
Trusted services exception for Azure services
Private endpoint = private IP in your VNet
Add your own IP to browse data in the portal

handsOn.title: Lock a storage account to your IP address
handsOn.cost: Cents. A few small files in a Standard LRS account cost almost nothing; delete the account at the end.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.
A storage account in rg-az104-lab: Standard performance, LRS redundancy, default settings. Name it st<yourinitials><number> (lowercase letters and numbers only, globally unique).

steps.do: Open the storage account > Data storage > Containers > + Container, name: docs. Upload any small text file.
steps.see: The file listed in the docs container.

steps.do: Open Security + networking > Networking. Under Public network access choose 'Enabled from selected virtual networks and IP addresses'. Do not add anything yet. Save.
Wait a minute, then open Containers > docs again.
steps.see: An error such as 'This request is not authorized to perform this operation'. The firewall now blocks your browser too.

steps.do: Back in Networking, under Firewall tick 'Add your client IP address'. Save, wait a minute, and open docs again.
steps.see: The file is visible again: your IP is allowed.

steps.do: Under Exceptions, read 'Allow Azure services on the trusted services list to access this storage account'.
steps.see: The box is ticked by default.

steps.do: Set Public network access back to 'Enabled from all networks'. Save.

check: You saw your own access blocked and restored by an IP rule.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
